Backup and migration

Moving data into AWS and backing up what is already there.

1. Core Concept

  • Network bandwidth is limited. If moving data over the wire takes years, AWS sends physical trucks (Snow). If syncing files continuously, use DataSync. AWS Backup centralizes snapshot orchestration.

2. Key Services & Features

  • AWS DataSync:
    • Agent-based transfer service.
    • Syncs on-premises NFS/SMB to S3, EFS, or FSx over Direct Connect/VPN.
    • Automates scheduling and validation.
  • AWS Snow Family:
    • Snowcone: 8 TB, ships via mail.
    • Snowball Edge: 80 TB, includes compute.
    • Snowmobile: 100 PB, literally an 18-wheeler truck.
    • Bypasses the internet completely.
  • AWS Backup:
    • Centralized backup policies (plans) across multiple services.
    • Supports cross-region and cross-account automated backups.
    • Governed by Organizations.

3. Architecture Rules

  • If the math shows internet transfer takes longer than 1 week, you must use a Snowball device.
  • Use AWS Backup to guarantee enterprise-wide compliance RPO/RTO across EBS, RDS, and EFS.

4. Scenarios & Use Cases

  • Migrating 500 Terabytes of data from a remote data center with a 10 Mbps connection.
    • Choose: Multiple Snowball Edge devices.
    • Why: Transferring 500TB over 10Mbps takes years. Physical transport takes days.
  • Continuously replicate an on-premises NAS to Amazon EFS for a hybrid cloud deployment.
    • Choose: AWS DataSync.
    • Why: It is optimized for fast, scheduled, over-the-wire synchronization to AWS storage.

Q5 Your customer wishes to deploy an enterprise application to AWS which will consist of several web servers, several application servers and a small (50GB) Oracle database information is stored, both in the database and the file systems of the various servers. The backup system must support database recovery whole server and whole disk restores, and individual file restores with a recovery time of no more than two hours. They have chosen to use RDS Oracle as the database. Which backup architecture will meet these requirements?
  • A Backup RDS using automated daily DB backups Backup the EC2 instances using AMIs and supplement with file-level backup to S3 using traditional enterprise backup software to provide file level restore.
  • B Backup RDS using a Multi-AZ Deployment Backup the EC2 instances using Amis, and supplement by copying file system data to S3 to provide file-level restore.
  • C Backup RDS using automated daily DB backups Backup the EC2 instances using EBS snapshots and supplement with file-level backups to Amazon Glacier using traditional enterprise backup software to provide file-level restore.
  • D Backup RDS database to S3 using Oracle RMAN Backup the EC2 instances using Amis, and supplement with EBS snapshots for individual volume restore.
Answer: A

  • D Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Turn on the EBS fast snapshot restore feature on the EBS snapshots. Restore the snapshots into new EBS volumes. Attach the new EBS volumes to EC2 instances in the test environment.
